rounding: Percents to one decimal (73.2% means 0.732). Spearman to three decimals. Full precision is in eval_snapshots/.

human_leaderboard.how_to_read: LR-Bench is pairwise accuracy: share of A-vs-B pairs the method gets right (chance 50%; ties skipped). CMU is mean Spearman correlation of the method's ranking vs 1-5 self-ratings (n=58 people).

rows.method: TF-IDF (word overlap; rare words count more)
Frozen SPECTER2 (average each person's paper stamps, then compare)
rows.notes: Headline SPECTER2 recipe. Closest-paper and top-3 pooling did not beat this on LR-Bench plus CMU together.

rows.method: First pass (SPECTER2 plus small add-on), trained on homemade citation key
Second pass tree, citation clues off (fair copy)
rows.notes: On human tests this scores a tiny list the humans already gave, not a search of 15,000 people then a reorder of 100.

rows.method: Second pass tree, citation clues off, trained on recency+topic+method homemade key
rows.trained_on: SimCite with recency, topic, and method knobs

rows.method: Language-model votes as a standalone scorer (gpt-4o-mini)
rows.notes: Different n than SPECTER2 on LR-Bench (ties skipped). A wash, not a win. Standalone pair scores, not votes fed into the tree on the last 15 names.

catalog_quiz.what: Homemade answer key: authors of similar papers this one cited. Did at least one of those people appear in the top 10 names? 1500 held-out catalog papers, ~15000 people.

ceiling.meaning: Share of papers where a homemade right person was already in the first pass's 100 names. The second pass cannot beat this.
